messages.text: Will it be a Sabalenka 'three-peat' or maiden US Open for new No 1 Rybakina?

metadata.summary: Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka is looking to become the first woman to achieve the 'three-peat' in New York since Serena Williams in 2014 but she faces incoming world No 1 Elena Rybakina in the US Open final on Saturday.
metadata.content: US Open: Will it be a 'three-peat' for Aryna Sabalenka or a maiden title in New York for new No 1 Elena Rybakina? | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis US Open: Will it be a 'three-peat' for Aryna Sabalenka or a maiden title in New York for new No 1 Elena Rybakina? Can Aryna Sabalenka make it a hat-trick of titles in New York or will incoming world No 1 Elena Rybakina deny her and claim a third Grand Slam?; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app By Raz Mirza at Flushing Meadows, New York Friday 11 September 2026 20:58, UK Image: Aryna Sabalenka and Elena Rybakina will battle it out in the US Open final on Saturday - live on Sky Sports Tennis Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka is looking to become the first woman to achieve the 'three-peat' in New York since Serena Williams in 2014 but she faces incoming world No 1 Elena Rybakina in the US Open final on Saturday. Rybakina's results this year, starting with her Australian Open final triumph against Sabalenka, will see her rise to the top of the rankings on Monday, ending the Belarussian's 99-week reign. But Sabalenka can exact some revenge for both that defeat and being overtaken at the WTA summit by defending her US Open title against Rybakina in Saturday's Flushing Meadows final - live on Sky Sports Tennis from 5pm. messages.text: Remarkable Razaullah knock denies England series sweep inside three days

metadata.summary: England were denied a series sweep of Pakistan inside three days of the final Test at Edgbaston after a remarkable display of six-hitting from 21-year-old Razaullah late on Friday.
metadata.content: England vs Pakistan: Razaullah, 21, hits remarkable 81 off 63 balls featuring nine sixes to force final Test into fourth day | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content England vs Pakistan: Razaullah, 21, hits remarkable 81 off 63 balls featuring nine sixes to force final Test into fourth day Dan Lawrence dismisses Razaullah (81 off 63 balls) with what proves to be the last ball of day three; Pakistan all out for 449 after battling second innings; England set 130 to win on day four - watch live on Sky Sports Cricket from 10.15am, Saturday By David Currie at Edgbaston Friday 11 September 2026 20:10, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day three of the third Test between England and Pakistan at Edgbaston England were denied a series sweep of Pakistan inside three days of the final Test at Edgbaston after a remarkable display of six-hitting from 21-year-old Razaullah late on Friday. Pakistan enjoyed easily their finest day of what's otherwise been a dismal series but were still trailing by two when their eighth wicket fell early into the evening session, only for Razaullah to smash 81 off just 63 deliveries, clearing the ropes a staggering nine times to equal Tim Southee's record for a debutant. The high-speed corners at the new track in Madrid are putting a lot of energy into the tyres, particularly the banked 'La Monumental' Turn 12 where the drivers carry huge speed on a 13.5-degree baking. Russell topped first practice and his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli was fastest in second practice with Saturday's qualifying at 3pm, live on Sky Sports F1, set to be crucial given the expected difficulty of overtaking in the race. metadata.summary: Durham clinched promotion to Division One of the Rothesay County Championship with a 93-run victory over Middlesex at Chester-le-Street.
metadata.content: County Championship: Ben Stokes back in top flight as Durham promoted after victory over Middlesex | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content County Championship: Ben Stokes back in top flight as Durham promoted after victory over Middlesex Durham complete return to domestic cricket's top flight by beating Middlesex with Callum Parkinson and Brydon Carse claiming four wickets apiece; Olly Stone took five as Nottinghamshire beat Hampshire and JT Langridge did likewise as Gloucestershire beat Lancashire Stuart Hodge @Hodgeythehack Friday 11 September 2026 17:32, UK Image: Brydon Carse (left) and Ben Stokes (right) in County Championship cricket action for Durham (PA Images) Durham clinched promotion to Division One of the Rothesay County Championship with a 93-run victory over Middlesex at Chester-le-Street. The north-east side began the final day needing eight wickets and Kasey Aldridge struck with the first ball to set the tone. Despite a battling unbeaten ton from Harry Duke alongside Ben Geddes' half-century, Durham took control with the ball as Callum Parkinson finished with four wickets for 45 runs and Brydon Carse also claimed four to secure their spot back in the top flight next year. messages.text: Caballo De Mar bounces back to form in Doncaster Cup

metadata.summary: Caballo De Mar bounced back from disappointing efforts at Royal Ascot and York to win the Betfred Howards Wright Doncaster Cup.
metadata.content: Doncaster Cup: George Scott's Caballo De Mar bounces back to form in Town Moor Group 2 | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Doncaster Cup: George Scott's Caballo De Mar bounces back to form in Town Moor Group 2 Caballo De Mar bounced back from disappointment at York with a decisive victory in the Doncaster Cup; Also on the card, Final Objective got up in the final strides to deny Crownbreaker in the Flying Childers Stakes Friday 11 September 2026 15:54, UK Image: Caballo De Mar won the Doncaster Cup under Oisín Murphy Caballo De Mar bounced back from disappointing efforts at Royal Ascot and York to win the Betfred Howards Wright Doncaster Cup. Questions had been raised over whether the five-year-old still had the stomach for the fight after coming home last in the Gold Cup and stopping quickly before finishing fourth in the Lonsdale Cup at York. But after taking up the running a furlong from home on Town Moor under Oisín Murphy, the George Scott-trained stayer proved his doubters wrong, pulling away from Beylerbeyi to land odds of 5-6 favourite by a length and a quarter. The race had been robbed of its likely favourite after Queenstown was pulled out and there was also drama beforehand when the Emmet Mullins-trained Winday gave trouble at the start. Having worked himself up into a sweat, he failed to the fire in the race itself, finishing a tailed off last of seven.
